about: HARBOUR CARDS OF THE RHINELAND AND FLANDERS: Colonia, Mogontia, Diusburg, Ganda, Andoverpis (Design/content/BRIEF.md, BRIEF_2.md). Written 6 October 2026 with the weave of the five places files; a draft in the game's own files, for the user to overwrite. Each card is tied to its port with port.id and listed in its site's 'do' in Data/places/<port>.json. Every *_key has real words in Data/writing/rhineland_flanders.json; an option's 'note' names the writing key of its outcome, and art.<card id> says what the picture shows. Flags: the spine's thread flags (sx_, hy_, sw_, bk_, sv_, ms_, df_, en_, bs_) for the steps they name; the rest take their port's name as a prefix. (?) in a note marks what is not attested.

cards.note: The spine's hook for hungry_years at Colonia: the king's estate (Deutz) sells his own grain below the top price, and the steward wants hulls. Synod of Frankfurt 794 c. 4 (the king's own barley one penny the modius, other men's two at most; chronicle_793.json 794-06-01-frankfurt-prices), so the steward names his price only from 794; the famine of 792-794 and the hunger of 805-807. Wido is places/colonia.json colonia.wido. The barley is delivered by harbour.andoverpis.thin_ale; the wheat is loaded by harbour.mogontia.kings_wheat. A sack is about a modius and a half (goods_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 808))
cards.title: Hulls for the king's grain
cards.intention: A big sunburnt man with a bundle of tally sticks is walking down the strand toward your boat, already talking. The king's barley is in the barn at Deutz, and the bread is short on the Scheldt.

options.label: Load the ten sacks for Andoverpis
Hand over the wheat from Mogontia
Tell him the hold is spoken for

memory.carry: carried the king's barley for him
memory.wheat: brought the Mogontia wheat down whole
memory.refuse: would not carry the king's grain

cards.note: The spine's hook for black_stones at Colonia: Mayen quern roughouts come down the Rhine, and a stone dealer wants to know what length the English king asked for. Charles's letter to Offa of 796 (the black stones and the cloaks; that the stones were querns is one reading (?)). Meginher is places/colonia.json colonia.meginher. The true measure is had from someone who enforces the ban (the thread's flag bs_ban_heard) or after the peace (bs_peace).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and year < 800 and not flag.colonia_measure_done
cards.title: A hand-breadth either way
cards.intention: A heavy man grey with stone dust sits among stacks of round black stones, a notched stick across his knees. He has two hundred querns roughed out for the English, and the English ports are shut.

options.label: Lay the measure you were given on his stack
Give him a width of your own
Promise to ask on the Thames

memory.guess.success: gave him a width that held
memory.promise: promised to ask on the Thames

cards.note: The spine's hook for saxon_end at Colonia: the archbishop is the king's arch-chaplain and his clerks hold the lists. Sets the thread's flag sx_brother_trail (Brunger's brother, given in 785). Hrotbert is places/colonia.json colonia.hrotbert; the story is colonia.names_on_the_list. The Old Saxon baptismal vow is texts_793.json saxon_vow. That a roll of 785 lay at Colonia is the game's (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and year < 806 and not flag.colonia_roll_read
cards.title: The names on the list
cards.intention: At the river gate a thin clerk sits in the shade with a wax tablet. In the chest behind him are the king's rolls: every Saxon hostage who has come down the river since the first submission, and in whose keeping.

options.label: Ask in the old priest's name
Carry the bishop's letters to Traiectum for it
Leave the lists in their chest

memory.priest: asked in the old priest's name
memory.letters: carried the bishop's letters for a sight of the roll

cards.note: The spine's hook for silver_road at Colonia: a mint and the archbishop's clerks, new coin for old at the king's rate, and a clerk who reads out the Frankfurt rule to anyone who argues. Synod of Frankfurt 794 c. 5 (chronicle_793.json 794-06-frankfurt-new-denier). Pennies of Charles for Colonia (dossier). The bag is delivered by harbour.mogontia.moneyer; the story is colonia.one_weight. The lesson sets the thread's flag sv_scale. The clerk speaks of the moneyer at Dorestad, so the card ends with Dorestad (gone after 863: ports_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and year >= 794 and year < 864 and not flag.colonia_mint_bag and not flag.colonia_mint_done
cards.title: One weight in every market
cards.intention: In the cellar that is the king's mint a clerk reads from a tablet to a man who is arguing about a penny. When the man has gone the clerk turns to you, a small sealed bag in his hand.

options.label: Take the sealed bag up to Mogontia
Pay him to show you the nick and the touchstone
Say the river is long and bags get wet

memory.carry: took the sealed bag for Mogontia
memory.lesson: paid for the lesson with the nick

cards.note: A riddle given: riddles_793.json riddle_symphosius_11_nix ('a schoolmaster of the cathedral', Colonia; Symphosius 11, Nix, ed. Riese 1894: 'Pulvis aquae tenuis'; the plain English in the line is ours). A text wanted: Alcuin's letter on Lindisfarne (texts_793.json alcuin_793). The spine's book_road: the schools of Colonia and Mogontia trade copies with England. 175 books at Saint Peter's in 833 (dossier).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and not flag.colonia_snow_given
cards.title: The dust of water
cards.intention: In Saint Peter's, under the scaffolding, a master is teaching six boys by the light of the west window. He has seen you looking at the book chest and waves you over without stopping the lesson.

options.label: Let him copy the York letter
Take the riddle and a seat with the boys
Say you only came to hear Mass

memory.copy: lent him the York letter to copy
memory.riddle: sat a lesson with his boys

cards.note: The spine's hook for swords_north at Colonia: the smiths' street; a blade may be sold to a count's man and to no stranger; a dealer who asks no questions wants silver by weight, not coin. Capitulary of Herstal 779 c. 20; Thionville 805 c. 7. Bero is places/colonia.json colonia.bero; the story is colonia.iron_at_dusk. The bundle is delivered by harbour.diusburg.east_road, which sets sw_ran_blades or sw_marked. With swords aboard, the toll man's own card offers its 'hide' option at every Frankish toll on the way.
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and year < 901 and not flag.colonia_bero_bundle and not flag.colonia_told_clerk
cards.title: Iron at dusk
cards.intention: At the quiet end of the smiths' row one shed is closed with hurdles. A spare man with burn-scarred arms is waiting by it as the light goes, a long bundle wrapped in greased wool on the anvil block beside him.

options.label: Take the bundle for Diusburg
Tell him you carry wine and stones
Tell the clerk at the gate what is behind the hurdles

memory.carry: carried a bundle for him and kept quiet
memory.tell: told the clerk about the closed shed

cards.note: A commission. The boat bank is places/colonia.json colonia.boat_bank (no yard is recorded: the game's (?)). The boat with two cabins that Bishop Hadebald gave Harald and Anskar in 826: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 7 (tr. Robinson 1921). Moss and tar for caulking river craft: Design/content/ships.md.
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia
cards.title: Moss and tar
cards.intention: On the bank below Saint Kunibert's a barge lies on rollers with her side planks off. The wright has the bishop's river boat to caulk before the water drops, and an empty tar trough.

options.label: Take his order for tar
Sell him a coil of rope from your hold
Watch him split a log, and ask about the river

cards.note: A passenger to carry and a text given. The spine's hook for saxon_end at Colonia: the king's crossing place; in 799 and 804 whole villages wait on the bank to be moved into Francia, and a priest reads them the vow again (Annales regni Francorum 799, 804; chronicle_793.json). The vow is texts_793.json saxon_vow. Erkanbert is places/colonia.json colonia.erkanbert (he dies in 810). Carrying them gently opens the clerk's roll (harbour.colonia.the_roll).
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and (year = 799 or year = 804)
cards.title: The vow, read again
cards.intention: The bank by the Deutz ferry is full of Saxon households sitting on their bundles under guard, waiting to be moved into Francia. An old red-faced priest is reading to them from a small book, in their own tongue.

options.label: Take the old woman and five children upriver for nothing
Hire the boat to the king's officer instead
Buy bread for them at the tower and go

memory.gently: carried the old and the children for nothing
memory.officer: hired his boat to the king's officer
memory.bread: bought bread for the people on the bank

cards.note: A person of the place with memory, and a rumour that is true (the price of Rhenish pots at Colonia falls for forty days). Adaltrud is places/colonia.json colonia.adaltrud; the house is the game's (?). Badorf ware from the Vorgebirge villages with Colonia its market (de.wikipedia Badorfer Keramik). Her quarrel with Ratburg of Mogontia is the weave's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia
cards.title: The ale-house in the tower
cards.intention: Smoke goes up into the hollow of a Roman wall tower. On the benches round the curve of the wall sit boatmen, a dice cup and a dog; a tall woman with a ladle looks you over once.

options.label: Pay for the round and listen
Drink on a tally stick
Settle the old stick

cards.note: A funeral. Burial by the saints outside the walls, in the old Roman cemeteries; Saint Gereon, 'at the Golden Saints', and the soldiers of the Theban Legion (de.wikipedia St. Gereon, by way of the dossier). Hauling by rope from the bank: Wandalbert, Miracula sancti Goaris. The drowned hauler is invented. The old priest is Erkanbert (colonia.erkanbert), who dies in 810.
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia
cards.title: A grave at the Golden Saints
cards.intention: Outside the north-west corner of the wall, among Roman tombs and cabbage plots, six boatmen are carrying a seventh on a plank. He went under a barge on the tow below the town. The strand has shut its doors for an hour.

options.label: Take a corner of the plank
Give twelve pennies for a Mass and the grave
Stand at the back with your cap off

memory.carry: helped carry a drowned hauler to his grave
memory.mass: paid for a hauler's Mass and grave

cards.note: A riddle given: riddles_793.json riddle_aldhelm_40_piper, held by 'a dealer in Rhenish glass' at Colonia, the last link of the set salt_to_pepper (Aldhelm, Enigma 40, Piper, ed. Ehwald 1919: 'Sum niger exterius rugoso cortice tectus'; the plain English is ours). It is given when the glass-cup riddle from Mogontia is solved (places/mogontia.json mogontia.born_in_the_furnace). Liutwin is places/colonia.json colonia.wine_factor. Glass beakers from the Rhine at Dorestad and Birka.
cards.when: moored and port.id = colonia and not flag.colonia_pepper_given
cards.title: Green glass
cards.intention: On the market's best pitch a tall narrow man sells wine from the cask and, from a chest of bran, green glass beakers to drink it from. The potter's widow on the next pitch is explaining loudly what glass is for.

options.label: Give the answer and take the leaf
Buy a crate of green beakers for the north
Taste, praise it, and buy nothing

memory.leaf: answered the glass riddle and took the leaf

cards.note: A riddle given: riddles_793.json riddle_aldhelm_80_calix_vitreus, held by 'a Frisian wine shipper of the Frisian quarter' at Mogontia, the third link of the set salt_to_pepper (Aldhelm, Enigma 80, Calix vitreus, ed. Ehwald 1919; the plain English is ours). It follows the wine-cask riddle had at Herio. Folcbald is places/mogontia.json mogontia.folcbald; the story is mogontia.born_in_the_furnace. The cloaks: Notker, Gesta Karoli I.34. Wine bespoken at the vintage is collected by harbour.mogontia.martinmas. Frisian traders on the Mainz shore: Landesmuseum Mainz; Annales Fuldenses 886.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year < 823
cards.title: The cask he does not sell
cards.intention: Under the Roman wall a cellar door stands open on casks two deep. A spare Frisian with a tasting cup at his belt is chalking a tally on the door post, and has seen your rope-burned hands.

lines.when: month >= 8 and month <= 10 and not flag.mogontia_wine_bespoken

options.label: Answer the cask riddle and ask for the leaf
Leave ninety pennies for two casks at Martinmas
options.check: month >= 8 and month <= 10 and silver >= 90 and not flag.mogontia_wine_bespoken

options.label: Sit, and drink what he pours

memory.bespeak: left silver for wine at the vintage

cards.note: A feast day: Martinmas, 11 November (Feasts.On), the day the new wine is ready and the Frisians go downriver with it (Design/research_trade_seasons_and_hints.md). The goose at Martinmas is an old custom whose age is not checked (?). The bridge that burned in May 813: Einhard, Life of Charles 32. Ratburg and Folcbald are places/mogontia.json.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and feast and month = 11
cards.title: New wine by Martinmas
cards.intention: It is Saint Martin's day. The bishop's church is full, every cask on the Frisians' shore has a spigot in it, and the haulers who brought you up the river are owed their feast.

options.label: Roll your two casks down to the boat
Stand the haulers their feast
Hear the feast's Mass at Saint Martin's and go to bed

cards.note: An oath: surety sworn before the bishop. The spine's hook for saxon_end at Mogontia: about 805 the hostages kept in the south are ordered brought here at mid-Lent; Brunger's brother is on the list (sets sx_brother_found; the night road also sets sx_carried_fugitive). Indiculus obsidum Saxonum Moguntiam deducendorum, MGH Capitularia I no. 115 (?). Otbert and Brunric are places/mogontia.json; the stories are mogontia.thirty_seven_names, colonia.names_on_the_list and diusburg.road_of_hostages; the endings by_leave, by_night and his_word are those of the Mogontia story. The surety of 120 d is the game's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year >= 804 and year < 807 and flag.sx_brother_trail and not flag.sx_brother_found
cards.title: Thirty-seven names
cards.intention: Mid-Lent in the bishop's hall. A row of men in borrowed cloaks stands before the clerk's table to be counted. The twenty-ninth has a scar through his left eyebrow, and the mate, in the doorway, has stopped breathing.

options.label: Stand surety before the bishop and take him home openly
Take him aboard after dark and be gone under the piers
Carry his word and a lock of his hair, and leave him his vines

memory.leave: stood surety for a hostage before the bishop
memory.night.success: took a hostage off the list by night
memory.night.failure: was caught taking a hostage by night

cards.note: The spine's hook for hungry_years ('also at Mogontia'): the king's estates sell his grain below the cap and want hulls; a dealer offers more than the cap for delivery after dark (sets hy_sold_dear); the public modius (sets hy_new_measure). Synod of Frankfurt 794 c. 4 (wheat four pennies the modius, the king's own at three); in 793, before the synod, the clerk speaks of the king's price and names no figure. Otbert is places/mogontia.json mogontia.otbert; the wheat is counted off by harbour.colonia.stewards_hulls, which sets hy_fed_poor. Mainz grain merchants on the Main: Einhard, Translation (tr. Wendell 1926).
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 808))
cards.title: The king's wheat
cards.intention: Grain boats lie three deep off the mouth of the Main. On the gravel the bishop's clerk is listing hulls; behind a jetty post a man in a good cloak holds up four fingers and looks at the river.

options.label: Go on the list: eight sacks for Colonia
Set four sacks down on the dealer's plot after dark
Have your own measure struck against the king's
Watch the measuring, and keep your hold for wine

memory.carry: went on the list of hulls for the king's wheat
memory.dark: sold wheat after dark above the king's price

cards.note: The spine's hook for silver_road ('also at Mogontia'). A Mainz penny of Charles's early type: Münzkabinett Berlin 18245022. The new penny and the fine of fifteen shillings: Frankfurt 794 c. 5. Madalger is places/mogontia.json mogontia.madalger; the bag comes from harbour.colonia.bad_pennies and the story is colonia.one_weight. Sets the thread's flag sv_scale.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year < 870
cards.title: Put it on the cloth
cards.intention: The ring of a hammer comes out into the street a beat late. Inside, a thick-set man with burn-scarred forearms is weighing pennies one by one over a cloth, and does not look up.

options.label: Hand over the sealed bag from Colonia
Ask him to teach you the scale and the nick
Change what foreign silver you have, and do not argue
Watch one penny struck, and go

memory.learn: learned the scale and the nick from him

cards.note: The spine's hooks for book_road: Liudger's new house at Werden needs a library from nothing ('also at Colonia and Mogontia, whose schools trade copies with England'). Sets the thread's flag bk_knows_worth; the book is delivered by harbour.diusburg.liudger, which sets bk_carried and bk_parchment. Lul of Mainz wrote to Wearmouth-Jarrow for Bede's works (?). Otbert is places/mogontia.json mogontia.otbert; the story is diusburg.books_up_the_ruhr. A book at 360 d is goods_793.json.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year >= 799 and year < 809 and not flag.mogontia_psalter_sent
cards.title: A psalter for the Ruhr
cards.intention: On the hill south of the wall the great church is rising round a small old one, and a school recites behind it. The bishop's clerk has a book wrapped in waxed linen on the table, and is looking at your hands.

options.label: Take the psalter for the Ruhr mouth
Ask him what a book is worth, and to whom
Tell him your hold leaks, which is true

memory.take: took a psalter to carry to the Ruhr
memory.teach: asked what a book is worth

cards.note: A commission. Riculf, archbishop 787-813, builder of Saint Alban's (consecrated 1 December 805), where Queen Fastrada was buried in August 794 (Annales Fuldenses 794; de.wikipedia 'Richulf', 'Stift St. Alban vor Mainz'). The comb he sent Alcuin about 796 and Alcuin's riddle in thanks: Things That Talk, after Sorrell (a paraphrase). He is places/mogontia.json mogontia.riculf; the three lines are its unlock mogontia.three_lines.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year < 814
cards.title: Lead for the hill
cards.intention: A lean bishop with lime dust on his hem is crossing the yard of Saint Martin's between two clerks, dictating to both. He stops when he sees a rope-scarred stranger, which is to say a boat.

options.label: Take his order for roofing lead
Sell him a cake of wax from your hold
Ask him for three lines to the bishop of Colonia
Bow, and let him get on

memory.lead: took his order for roofing lead
memory.wax: sold him wax for the altar
memory.lines: asked him for three lines to Colonia

cards.note: A hire, and a rumour that is true (the price of wine at Mogontia falls for sixty days). Ratburg is places/mogontia.json mogontia.ratburg; her house burns with the Frisians' shore in 886 (Annales Fuldenses). Hauling by rope from the bank 'as the custom is': Wandalbert, Miracula sancti Goaris. The Saxon hauler is invented; a crewman who has the tongue teaches a little of it (the engine's tongue verb).
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year < 887
cards.title: Rope hands
cards.intention: A long low house on the Frisians' shore, its door to the river. On the bench outside, haulers sit with their boots off and their feet in a tub. Inside, the ale-wife is pouring and has not stopped talking.

options.label: Give the Saxon a berth
Pay the score and ask what the Main men say
Sit with your feet in the tub and say nothing

memory.hire: hired a hauler from her bench
memory.news: paid his score and asked the news

cards.note: A lawsuit and an oath: a claim for a day's hauling heard at the river gate, settled by payment, by oath-helpers or by a neighbour's word, as Frankish custom had it (the oath with helpers: peoples/frankish.md; the false oath and the hand, capitulary of 802 c. 36). Hauling upriver by gangs and the halt at Saint Goar's cell: Wandalbert, Miracula sancti Goaris (about 839). The custom about lost days is invented in the period's manner (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia
cards.title: A day on the rope
cards.intention: Under the river gate the bishop's toll man is hearing a case from his bench, as he does most mornings. The master of the gang that hauled you through the gorge says you owe him a day more than you paid.

options.label: Pay the eight pennies
Swear with your crew that the gang lay drunk, not the river high
Ask a man of the shore to speak for you
Ask for the case to stand over until Martinmas

memory.pay: paid the gang's claim without an oath
memory.swear.success: swore the claim down with his crew
memory.swear.failure: swore an oath that did not hold

cards.note: Einhard, Life of Charles 17 and 32 (tr. Turner 1880): the timber bridge on the old piers, five hundred paces, ten years in the building, burned in three hours in May 813; the king meant to rebuild in stone. Begun about 803 and finished in 813 (de.wikipedia 'Rheinbrücke Karls des Großen', a reckoning from Einhard's ten years (?)): so the ferryman watches it being built from 803 and sees it stand only in the spring of 813. Notker I.30: rascals who robbed the boats that passed beneath. That ferrymen were blamed is a modern retelling, used only as town talk (places/mogontia.json, the story mogontia.three_hours, whose ending 'accident' this card's oath is). The ferryman is Ratburg's brother, unnamed.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and year >= 800 and year < 815
cards.title: The old piers
cards.intention: Twenty-one stone piers stand in a line across the river to Kastel, brown water piling against each. At the foot of the lane the ferryman is leaning on his pole, looking at them as a man looks at a neighbour's dog.

options.label: Go to the hall and swear what you saw: a fire from the middle, no boat near
Pay him three pennies to take you through the piers
Lean on the rail and let him talk

memory.swear: swore the bridge fire was mischance

cards.note: A fast day: Lent (the engine's 'fast', and March until the calendar carries the fasts). No flesh, milk or eggs in Lent; fish allowed. The spine's Brunger fears 'a priest asking what he ate in Lent'; eating flesh in Lent is a capital matter in the Saxon capitulary of about 785 (Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae c. 4, from memory (?)). The mid-Lent counting of the hostages about 805. Saint Alban's as church and monastery with guests: Einhard, Translation (tr. Wendell 1926).
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia and (fast or month = 3)
cards.title: Lenten fare
cards.intention: It is the fast before Easter. At the guest house on Saint Alban's hill the board is set with bread, beans, leeks and thin ale, and the guest-master is counting heads. Your mate is counting what is not on the table.

options.label: Keep the fast with the house, crew and all
Buy fish for the boat at the Lenten price
Eat with the house, and do not look into the boat after dark

memory.keep: kept the Lenten fast with the house

cards.note: A passenger to carry. Mainz grain merchants who boated grain down the Main and gave a blind man passage: Einhard, Translation of SS. Marcellinus and Peter (tr. Wendell 1926), for about 830, set a generation earlier here as places/mogontia.json does (mogontia.grain_merchant, Gundhart). The Golden Saints at Colonia: Saint Gereon. The pilgrim is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = mogontia
cards.title: A seat going down
cards.intention: By the sacks of Main wheat in the market a big floury man is talking to a pilgrim with a staff and a white stare. The pilgrim is blind. He wants to pray at the Golden Saints at Colonia before winter.

options.label: Give him the seat for nothing
Take his six pennies
Say the boat is full of casks

memory.free: gave a blind pilgrim passage for nothing

cards.note: A passenger to carry. The spine's hook for saxon_end at Diusburg: the Hellweg meets the Rhine; hostages and deported families come down it on foot under guard, and an officer wants hulls to carry them upriver (Annales regni Francorum 794-804; chronicle_793.json). Raginhard is places/diusburg.json diusburg.raginhard; the story is diusburg.road_of_hostages. Feeding them counts with the priest at Colonia (colonia_carried_gently opens harbour.colonia.the_roll). The fee is the game's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and year < 806
cards.title: Twelve, sitting down
cards.intention: A line of Saxons sits on the mud under the hill with bundles and children, two spearmen over them. The king's steward, tally sticks in his fist, is looking at your boat and counting benches.

options.label: Carry the twelve to Colonia for the king's silver
Carry them, and feed them from your own stores
Tell him the boat is a wine boat

memory.carry: carried hostages to Colonia at the full count

cards.note: Sets the thread's flag sx_brother_trail (saxon_end: 'set on the Rhine or at Daventre'). Hathuswith is places/diusburg.json diusburg.hathuswith, a hostage of 785 kept in the court kitchen (the spine's placing of hostages at this estate). She is reached through the ale-wife (harbour.diusburg.boatmans_tale sets diusburg_gerlind_sent and leads here). The role is 'hostage', a woman.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and year < 806 and not flag.sx_brother_trail and flag.diusburg_gerlind_sent
cards.title: A pot on
cards.intention: The court kitchen is a low hall full of smoke at the top of the hill. A tall fair woman with a wooden cross worn outside her dress is stirring a pot big enough to wash a child in, and does not turn round.

options.label: Ask her plainly about a boy of thirteen with a split eyebrow
Leave a sack of salt for her kitchen, and ask nothing today
Thank her for the bread and go

memory.ask: asked her about the Weser boys

cards.note: A rumour that is not true (the salt boats; salt at Mogontia is unchanged) and, in 810, one that is: the emperor's elephant Abul Abaz died at Lippeham, a day downstream, when the host mustered against Godfred (Annales regni Francorum 810; chronicle_793.json 810-summer-elephant-dies), the spine's hook for godfreds_market at Diusburg. Gerlind is places/diusburg.json diusburg.gerlind. The rocks below Saint Goar's cell: Wandalbert, Miracula sancti Goaris. The option 'kitchen' goes on to harbour.diusburg.kitchen.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg
cards.title: Said a second time
cards.intention: Under a green bush on a pole: one fire on the floor, boatmen at one end and road people at the other. A bargeman from upriver has the bench by the door and a story, and the ale-wife is watching him tell it.

options.label: Sell the boatman a sack of salt at his price
Ask the ale-wife what she thinks of his story
Go up to the court kitchen with her name
Drink, and keep your salt

memory.sell: sold salt cheap on a boatman's tale
memory.gerlind: asked her what she thought of the tale
memory.kitchen: went up to the kitchen with her name

cards.note: The spine's hooks for cross_and_grove and book_road at Diusburg: Liudger is buying land up the Ruhr for his own house of monks at Werden and wants books, a bell and glass; a first cargo of books up the Ruhr. Sets bk_carried and bk_parchment (the psalter comes from harbour.mogontia.psalter) and ms_carried_priest. Liudger: Werden about 799, bishop at Mimigernaford 30 March 805, died 26 March 809; the dream is Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri (?). He is cast.liudger (places/diusburg.json diusburg.liudger); the stories are diusburg.books_up_the_ruhr and diusburg.bell_and_spring.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and year >= 799 and year < 809
cards.title: Books up the Ruhr
cards.intention: At the Ruhr mouth a tall spare priest in a travel-stained cloak is leading his horse down to the ferry, a book satchel on his shoulder. He stops when he sees a Dorestad boat.

options.label: Hand over the psalter from Mogontia
Take his order for window glass from Colonia
Carry him up to Colonia to be made bishop
Ask his blessing on the boat and go

memory.glass: took his order for window glass

cards.note: The spine's hook for swords_north ('also at Mogontia and Diusburg, where the king's men watch the road east'). Capitulary of Herstal 779 c. 20; Thionville 805 c. 7 (the search of eastbound goods, half to the finder: chronicle_793.json). A sword with its scabbard at seven solidi (84 d): Lex Ribuaria 40 (36) c. 11. Sets sw_ran_blades or sw_marked. The bundle comes from harbour.colonia.iron_at_dusk; the story is diusburg.blades_on_the_east_road. The dealer is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and year < 901
cards.title: The east road
cards.intention: The smith by the road shoes horses. A man who is not a customer sits on the bench by his door; another, who lodges at the back, has something long wrapped in greased cloth and wants it gone before dinner is over.

options.label: Hand the Colonia bundle to the man at the back
Buy his two blades by weight, for the north
Give the dealer's name to the steward for the finder's half
Look at the river

memory.deliver.success: brought a bundle past the watch
memory.deliver.failure: was caught with a bundle of blades
memory.name: gave a dealer's name to the steward

cards.note: A riddle given: riddles_793.json riddle_exeter_16_anchor (Exeter Book riddle 16, 'Anchor'; text exeter_16_anchor, Tupper 1910), the unlock diusburg.anchor_riddle of places/diusburg.json. The iron is the lead stock of a Roman anchor stamped L V, found in the Rhine between Duisburg and Homberg in 1968 (Krause, Römische Ankerfunde). The lesson sets the flag diusburg_ruhr_water (the unlock diusburg.ruhr_water). Wolfhelm is diusburg.wolfhelm.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and year < 819
cards.title: Iron in the river
cards.intention: Where the Ruhr slides into the Rhine a wide flat ferry lies on a gravel spit. The ferryman, short and very broad, is sounding the mid-stream with a pole twice his height, and has just struck something that rings.

options.label: Take the pole and feel the thing for yourself
Pay him six pennies to show you the Ruhr once, slowly
Watch him work, and keep to the outside of the bend

memory.sound: sounded the iron in the river with him
memory.ruhr: paid to be shown the Ruhr

cards.note: A commission. Regino of Prüm, Chronicon 884 (ed. Kurze 1890): Northmen come up the Rhine with Godfrid's consent, take the stronghold of Diusburh, fortify it in their usual way and winter there; Duke Henry camps against them and lets them take no plunder; in spring they burn their camp and go. The spine's thread dorestad_falls; the story diusburg.winter_of_the_northmen (the endings lid_on_the_pot and both_camps). Henry is diusburg.henry. The offers are invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = diusburg and ((year = 883 and month >= 10) or (year = 884 and month <= 3))
cards.title: The lid on the pot
cards.intention: Burnt house posts under the hill. On the wooded height, a new palisade with long ships drawn up below it; across the Ruhr, the tents and horse lines of the duke's camp in the frost. Both have seen your sail.

options.label: Take the duke's order for oats
Row four sacks of oats to the alder bank after dark
Sell to neither, and go upstream

memory.duke: took the duke's order for oats
memory.fort.success: sold oats to the fort unseen
memory.fort.failure: was seen selling to the fort

cards.note: A riddle given and a text wanted: riddles_793.json riddle_symphosius_16_tinea, given by 'the librarian of Saint Bavo's' at Ganda (Symphosius 16, Tinea, ed. Riese 1894: 'Littera me pavit, nec quid sit littera novi'; the plain English is ours); Alcuin's letter on Lindisfarne (texts_793.json alcuin_793). Einold is places/ganda.json ganda.einold; the unlock is ganda.moth_riddle. In 793 the abbeys have canons, not monks; Saint Bavo's is burned in 851 (Annales Bertiniani).
cards.when: moored and port.id = ganda and year < 851
cards.title: What ate the words
cards.intention: In a side room of Saint Bavo's a book chest stands with its lid propped open to air. A round-shouldered canon with a quill behind his ear is turning leaves over one by one, looking for holes.

options.label: Take the riddle on a wax tablet
Tell him the answer
Let him mend his copy of the York letter from yours
Ask how he keeps the damp out

cards.note: Two commissions and a price word. Ansold is places/ganda.json ganda.cellarer; the stories are ganda.wool_before_shearing and (the Mass wine) the weave with mogontia.folcbald. 'The yield of honey has been small these two years' and the pack-load of wax are Einhard's letters (Monumenta Carolina 1867), a generation later; Einhard abbot of Blandinium from 815. The vineyard on the slope of the hill: nl.wikipedia Sint-Pietersabdij (Gent) (?). Saint Peter's is plundered in the winter of 879-80.
cards.when: moored and port.id = ganda and year < 879
cards.title: Counted twice
cards.intention: On the sand hill above the meeting of the rivers, at the cellar door of Saint Peter's, a thin cleric is counting cheeses onto a board and talking to nobody. He goes on counting when he sees you.

options.label: Take his order for wax
Take his order for the Mass wine
Count the cheeses with him, aloud

memory.wine: took his order for the Mass wine

cards.note: A feast day: Saint Bavo's Mass, 1 October, Ganda's own saint's day, when the dues come in (the spine's calendar; Einhard's letters send wax 'after the Mass of Saint Bavo'). The calendar of the game does not yet carry it, so the card comes in the tenth month. Hildrada is places/ganda.json ganda.hildrada; Bavo's Life (he sold his own people, and did penance led in chains): dossier 7. The host's list of 810-811: the story ganda.emperors_ships.
cards.when: moored and port.id = ganda and month = 10 and year < 851
cards.title: Saint Bavo's Mass
cards.intention: The first day of the vintage month: Saint Bavo's Mass. The dues are coming in by cart and barge from as far as the sea, the abbot's men are riding home, and every bench on the bank is taken.

options.label: Hear the Mass at the saint's tomb and leave two pennies
Sell to the abbot's men before they ride home
Take your bench and pay in news

memory.mass: heard Saint Bavo's Mass and gave
memory.sell: sold to the abbot's men at the feast
memory.bench: paid for his ale in news

cards.note: Two commissions. The spine's hook for godfreds_market at Ganda: in 811 the emperor comes to see the ships he ordered built against the Northmen; shipwrights, timber and pitch are wanted (Annales regni Francorum 811; chronicle_793.json 811-11-ghent-ships; the fleet ordered after the Danish raid on Frisia in 810). Hildgis is places/ganda.json ganda.hildgis; the story is ganda.emperors_ships (the endings in_the_hulls, sold_dear, stood_by). Oak comes from Diusburg (diusburg.raginhard).
cards.when: moored and port.id = ganda and ((year = 810 and month >= 7) or year = 811)
cards.title: Ships by the dark end of the year
cards.intention: The wrights' strand is ankle deep in chips. A row of keels stands on blocks, more than this bank has ever seen at once, and a broad man with two short fingers is swearing mildly at a plank of green oak.

options.label: Take his order for oak and pitch
Sell him the oak in your hold at the hurry's price
Sell him the oak at the common price
Carry nothing for the fleet

memory.order: took his order for the emperor's ships
memory.dear: sold him oak at the hurry's price
memory.fair: sold him oak at the common price

cards.note: A passenger to carry. The spine's hook for price_of_england at Ganda: the army that had sat at Fulham crosses from England and winters here, selling what was taken there (Annales Vedastini 879-881; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 880, Ingram 1823: 'to Ghent in Frankland, and sat there a year'; chronicle_793.json 879-11-ghent-army). It is not the army King Alfred beat, which the Chronicle sends from Cirencester to East Anglia in the same year. Sets en_followed_silver. Ketil is places/ganda.json ganda.ketil (invented; nobody of the army at Ghent is named); the story is ganda.winter_army. The clerk's line is John 1:1.
cards.when: moored and port.id = ganda and ((year = 879 and month >= 11) or year = 880 or (year = 881 and month >= 8))
cards.title: Sat there a year
cards.intention: The burned abbey has a bank and stakes round it and long ships in a row below. In the roofless church men sit among bales and chests and weigh silver on a folding scale. One of them gives you peace for the length of a bargain.

options.label: Buy the book whole, and the clerk with it
Buy plate by weight
Buy nothing, and go down by his peace

memory.book: bought a gospel book and its clerk out of the camp
memory.plate: bought church plate at the army's camp

cards.note: A deal and a commission. Comb-making from sawn stag skulls to the finished comb at Antwerp, the makers perhaps travelling men (Bellens 2021). Liafgrim is places/andoverpis.json andoverpis.liafgrim, who comes with the swallows and goes at Martinmas (so the card keeps to the months between); the story is andoverpis.stag_heads. The saw from Colonia is the weave's (colonia.bero).
cards.when: moored and port.id = andoverpis and year < 825 and month >= 4 and month <= 11
cards.title: Stag heads
cards.intention: Under a lean-to of hurdles, stag skulls hang by their eye-holes from a rail. A lean fair man sits astride a bench with a fine saw, the ground white with dust round his feet, and does not look up.

options.label: Give a bundle of antler for a dozen combs
Take his order for stag antler
Buy a dozen combs for silver
Sit out of his light and watch

cards.note: The spine's thread hungry_years: sets hy_fed_poor or hy_sold_dear. The famine of 792-794 and the false grain of 793 (chronicle_793.json 793-great-famine, 793-spring-false-grain); the top prices of Frankfurt 794 c. 4 (barley two pennies the modius, so about three the sack). Ermentrud and Hildulf are places/andoverpis.json; the story is andoverpis.thin_ale. The steward's barley comes from harbour.colonia.stewards_hulls. Pig bones 46 in a hundred in the digs (Bellens 2021).
cards.when: moored and port.id = andoverpis and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 808))
cards.title: Thin ale
cards.intention: On the selling bank nobody is selling grain. Poor people from up river sit along the wall of the big house and are given broth. The ale-wife stands at the front with a ladle and waits to hear what is in your sacks.

options.label: Hand over the steward's ten sacks at the king's price
Sell four sacks of your own barley at the king's price
Sell four sacks at what a hungry place will bear
You have no grain: ask what else would help

memory.kings: sold barley at the king's price in a hungry year
memory.dear: sold barley dear in a hungry year

cards.note: A feast day: Saints Peter and Paul, 29 June (Feasts.On), the feast of this church, in the week after Saint John's day. The church of Peter and Paul given to Willibrord in 726 'for incense and lights', with a third of the toll, and the curse at the end of the charter (Mertens and Torfs I, 1845). The book wanted is a Life of Willibrord (Alcuin's, written before 797 (?)): the story andoverpis.a_life_for_the_feast, whose unlock andoverpis.saints_third this gives; sets the thread's flag bk_carried. Hildulf is andoverpis.hildulf.
cards.when: moored and port.id = andoverpis and year < 819 and ((feast and month = 6) or hold.books > 0)
cards.title: Peter and Paul
cards.intention: The small timber church on the sand rise has its west door open to the river. Two lamps hang before the altar and one is not lit. The priest names the saint whose day it is before he says good morning.

options.label: Give him the book for his thirty pennies
Pay for oil for the second lamp
Stand through the Mass at the back

memory.book: gave him a book for his church

cards.note: An oath. The toll at Antwerp and the church's third of it: the charter of 20 October 726 (Mertens and Torfs I, 1845). The perjurer 'shall lose his right hand': capitulary of 802 c. 36 (Henderson 1892, by way of peoples/frankish.md). Adalwin and Hildulf are places/andoverpis.json; that they reckon at Michaelmas is their ties' (29 September, the usual term for dues (?)).
cards.when: moored and port.id = andoverpis and year < 815 and month >= 9 and month <= 10
cards.title: The stick and the door
cards.intention: At Michaelmas the toll man's notched stick is laid beside the priest's count of boats, made from the church door. They differ by one. Both men are looking at your boat.

options.label: Swear that you paid at the post, once, into his hand
Say only that the saint's third should not be short
Say you cannot remember one tide from another

memory.swear: swore to his count at the toll post

cards.note: The spine's hook for dorestad_falls at Andoverpis: in 836 the Northmen burn the landing on the Scheldt ('Andwerpam civitatem'; no rampart stands there before about 900: places/andoverpis.json) in the same summer as Witla (Annales Fuldenses 836; Dorestad plundered 834, 835, 836: Annales Bertiniani). Sets the thread's flag df_warned. Ansgard is places/andoverpis.json andoverpis.ansgard; the story is andoverpis.the_sticks_first (the endings warned and bought_cheap). The count of Walcheren who counted spears is walichrum.eggihard.
cards.when: moored and port.id = andoverpis and ((year = 834 and month >= 7) or year = 835 or (year = 836 and month <= 6)) and not flag.andoverpis_warned
cards.title: How many sails
cards.intention: The big house on posts has a young ale-wife now, with her grandmother's tally sticks at her belt. She asks every skipper the same thing before she pours, and she is asking you.

options.label: Tell her plainly: they pass the river mouth every summer, and one flood would bring them here
Offer to carry her stores and the church's chest inland, for a fee
Say the Scheldt is wide and they have richer places to burn

memory.warn: warned her of the fleets before the fire
memory.fee: carried her stores inland for a fee
memory.calm: told her there was nothing to fear
